$comment: Parity policy for the shared VfSkeleton cases. Plain data: no DSL, no waiver engine. The component has no children and no interaction, so almost everything it can get wrong is an attribute.

classifications.exact: Must match literally across every target. Structure, canonical classes, native attributes, visible text, accessible names, computed geometry and colour.
classifications.semantic: Framework mechanics may differ; the observable meaning must not. How content is composed, how a renderer marks its own output.
classifications.framework-specific: Historical behaviour of one adapter that the other is not required to reproduce. Narrow, named, and covered by its own test.

notCompared.$comment: Recorded so a reviewer can see what is deliberately outside the comparison, without leaving dead dimensions that look like live protection. Nothing here is a waiver: the extractor never produces these differences in the first place.
notCompared.attributeOrder: Attributes are extracted into a sorted map, so serialisation order cannot produce a difference. It carries no meaning.
notCompared.rendererMarkers: Vue scope attributes (data-v-*) and the Razor ownership marker (data-vf-razor*) are dropped by scripts/parity/extract.mjs. They identify the renderer, not the product. Any other data-* attribute is compared as dom.productData.

dom.structure.description: An unexpected element, invalid wrapper arrangement, or tag mismatch. Never approvable; comparison continues through tag differences so meaningful attribute/child diagnostics remain visible.

dom.canonicalClasses.description: vf-* classes on every element. Consumer classes included, because where a consumer class lands relative to the canonical ones is part of the contract.

dom.nativeAttributes.description: class and style on the root div, plus any native attribute a consumer forwards. style is the contract here rather than incidental markup: the component writes min-height and border-radius itself and merges a consumer style over them.

dom.text.description: Visible text content of every element.

dom.aria.description: aria-* attributes and role. aria-hidden is the whole accessibility contract of this component, and the fact that a consumer can replace it is part of that contract.

dom.productData.description: data-* attributes that belong to the product rather than to a renderer.

style.geometry.description: Computed box metrics of every measured role.

style.colour.description: Computed colour, background and border colour of every measured role.

visual.description: Rendered screenshot of the case, per theme.

a11y.role.description: The role each measured node exposes in the accessibility tree, including exposing none.

a11y.name.description: The accessible name each measured node exposes, including exposing none.

a11y.states.description: Accessibility states exposed by each measured node.

static.noInteraction.description: The recorded fact that the component declares no interaction to drive, and that the harness measured this rather than skipping the stage. Includes the component-owned focusable and interactive-role counts, which for a skeleton are zero on every target.

historicalQuirks.description: animated defaults to true, so vf-skeleton--animated is on every skeleton unless a caller switches it off. Every modifier migrated before this one works the other way round.
historicalQuirks.reason: A port that copied the M15 'the default emits nothing' convention would ship a skeleton that never shimmers, and the static box would look correct.

historicalQuirks.description: radius="" does not round the corners to zero; Vue omits a style property whose value is '', so the declaration disappears and a skeleton with an empty radius and no min-height has no style attribute at all.
historicalQuirks.reason: Normalising the empty string into border-radius:0 would change what the stylesheet is allowed to decide.

historicalQuirks.description: aria-hidden is a static attribute on a component that does not set inheritAttrs: false, so an inherited attribute of the same name replaces it and aria-hidden="false" on a skeleton is reachable.
historicalQuirks.reason: Blocking the override would be a silent API removal. Both adapters let the consumer win.

historicalQuirks.description: minHeight accepts a number and appends px, so 0 becomes 0px rather than being dropped as falsy.
historicalQuirks.reason: Treating 0 as absent is the obvious defect and produces a placeholder with no reserved height.
